problems: Cliopatria draws the High Duke's Seniorate realm (Kraków, Łęczyca, Sieradz, western Kuyavia, Pomerelia) under the Greater Poland rows 1177-1187, 1202-1205 and 1227-1235 and under the Masovia rows 1147-1176; the dossiers replace them with the duchies' own land and carry the Seniorate as gain/loss events (Seniorate region = Greater Poland 1177 shape minus its 1139 shape). The Sandomierz dossier (eu-15-e) records at confidence 1 a 1199 Mieszko return and a 1227 hand-over to Greater Poland that the pages opened here do not support, and dates Konrad's Masovia to c. 1200 against 1199 here.

The Duchy of Łęczyca ends in July 1144 (Salomea's death) against Cliopatria's 1146; the duchy-of-silesia dossier has no matching 1144 gain, so 1145-1146 would be a 35-cell hole unless Silesia takes the land.

Greater Poland and Masovia union in Cliopatria's Duchy of Kuyavia row (1188-1205) and Duchy of Kalisz row (1210-1219) for years the pages give the land to them (Kuyavia 1173-1198/99 and from 1199-1205, Kalisz not theirs 1207-1217): the Kuyavia and Kalisz dossiers of other eu-15 parts will double-draw unless the colour agent decides; pages disagree on Kuyavia's passing (1198, 1199, 1205).

Cliopatria gives 11 south-eastern Masovian cells to the Mongol Empire in 1241-1249 (verdict adjust, a reading from the page's silence on Masovia) and 21 Masovian cells to the Teutonic Order in 1333-1343 (only the 8-cell Dobrzyń Land is on the pages, which say it went to Poland, not Masovia, in 1343): the mongol-empire, teutonic-order and kingdom-of-poland dossiers should agree.

Brandenburg's gain of Santok and Drezdenko is page-dated 1265 and 1270 against Cliopatria's 1272; Przemysł II's Kraków (1290) and Pomerelia (1294-1296) are not in the Cliopatria Greater Poland shapes (drawn under Grand Duchy of Kraków and Duchies of Poland) and the ledger events must not be applied on top of those rows without a decision.

Masovia's identity.end 1351 is Cliopatria's last shape; the duchy lasted to 1526 as a Polish fief, so the dissolve event is a map boundary (confidence 2). Greater Poland's 1304 dissolve is also a map boundary (confidence 1); the pages date Bohemian rule from 1300.

Wikipedia 'Mongol invasion of Poland' is a disambiguation page (no content); 'First Mongol invasion of Poland' was read instead. The en-dash and non-ASCII titles loaded when percent-encoded or written in UTF-8. Nineteen distinct pages were opened in all (22 source entries across the three dossiers, since the Testament and Casimir II pages are shared); no page failed to load. No Wikipedia infobox gave an area for any of the three states, so no area comparison was possible.

Months are given only where a page gives them; the three founding events of 1138 carry a month only for Łęczyca (Salomea of Berg page: Bolesław III died 28 October 1138). No subagent, hearthbot tool or git operation was used; scratch files are under /tmp/claude-0/work/research-eu-15-d/.
